title: Kilobytes to Terabytes
objective: After this level you can compare the sizes of a text message, a photo, a movie and a whole drive in bytes.
summary: Kilo, mega, giga and tera each mean 1,000 times more bytes: a text is dozens, a photo megabytes, an HD film gigabytes. A 1 TB drive shows as 931 GB in Windows.

cards.headline: A text message and a hard drive are measured in the same thing.
cards.body: Bytes, from Level 2: eight bits each. The only difference is how many. Kilo, mega, giga and tera are the counting words, and the jumps between them are bigger than they sound.

cards.headline: Every step is a thousand times bigger
cards.body: Storage borrows the metric prefixes: kilo means a thousand, mega a million, giga a billion and tera a trillion. So a kilobyte is about 1,000 bytes, and each step up is 1,000 times the last. A typed character takes about one byte, so a short text of a few dozen characters is a few dozen bytes. A single megabyte could hold thousands of them.

cards.headline: A photo and a film, in bytes

items.label: One photo
points: 3 bytes per pixel: about 73 MB raw
JPEG at 20 to 1, still looking sharp: about 3.6 MB

items.label: One film
points: HD streaming: up to 3 GB an hour
A two-hour film: up to 6 GB
Over a thousand saved photos' worth

cards.fact: A 1 TB drive really holds a trillion bytes. Windows shows about 931 GB.
cards.context: Drive makers count in thousands: 1 TB is 1,000,000,000,000 bytes. Windows counts in powers of two, so its gigabyte is 1,073,741,824 bytes, which is 1,024 × 1,024 × 1,024. Divide one by the other and you get about 931. No bytes went missing. The two sides just count in different-sized buckets.

mascot.line: People mix these up all the time. Same bytes, different-sized buckets.

cards.headline: Sizes: measured
learned: Kilo, mega, giga, tera: each step is 1,000 times bigger
A typed character is about one byte
A photo is megabytes; an HD film is gigabytes
A 1 TB drive shows about 931 GB because Windows counts in 1,024s

questions.prompt: By Netflix's figures, how much data can an hour of HD streaming use?

options.label: About 3 KB
options.rationale: That is only about 3,000 typed characters.

options.label: About 3 MB
options.rationale: That is about one photo saved as JPEG.

options.label: About 3 TB
options.rationale: That is three whole 1 TB drives.

questions.explanation: HD streaming uses up to 3 GB an hour, so a two-hour film is up to 6 GB.

questions.prompt: A new 1 TB drive shows up in Windows as about 931 GB. What explains the gap?

options.label: Hidden system files take up about 69 GB
options.rationale: The gap comes from counting, not from files.

options.label: The maker rounded its label up to sell more
options.rationale: The drive really holds a trillion bytes.

options.label: Windows counts each gigabyte as 1,073,741,824 bytes
Drives lose space as soon as they are switched on
options.rationale: No bytes go missing at all.

questions.explanation: The maker counts a trillion bytes; Windows divides by its bigger, 1,024-based gigabyte and gets about 931.

questions.prompt: Level 2 says a byte is 8 bits. About how many bits are in a 1 KB file of about 1,000 bytes?

options.label: About 125
options.rationale: That divides by 8 instead of multiplying.

options.label: About 256
options.rationale: That is the number of patterns in one byte.

questions.explanation: About 1,000 bytes times 8 bits each is about 8,000 bits.
